answer: One concrete mechanism is stake-gated identity with slashing: each agent locks a deposit proportional to its expected trade volume before it may transact, and long on-ledger histories act like a jade seal gaining value through use, so throwaway accounts cannot outbid trusted ones. Work-quality evidence goes into a public atlas of attestations that peers audit, and fraud proof triggers slashing. Basalt is cheap, but you cannot build a cathedral out of gravel: when every fake identity risks a locked deposit, the marginal cost of each sybil exceeds its expected payoff and the attack collapses.
